content.comment_body: Hello! How can I create an asynchronous pulse generator with a time format like 00:00 in the [product_name] Web Editor? How should I enter this in the VM mapping parameters, and how is it done in the Web Editor?

In the [product_name] Web Editor, you can't create an asynchronous pulse generator—only in the [product_name] Soft Comfort. With the Web Editor, you can adjust pulse and interpulse values. What do you mean by the format 00:00?
I want it to appear in the Web Editor as shown in photo 1. What should I enter in photo 2 and what in photo 3? Sorry, my English isn't great. Thank you for your quick reply!

The selection you made in photo 2 is correct—just use free VW numbers. In the Web Editor, use scale time instead of analog value, select the right time unit (hours, minutes, seconds), and enter the VW number.

Do you only want to display the values in the Web Editor or also allow changes within the Web Editor? The issue is that the [product_name] doesn't process times in the 00:00 format—it only displays them that way. For example, a timer showing 2 min and 49 sec as 02:49 m is actually stored as 169 (seconds) in the [product_name].

If you use a scaled time as suggested by [user_name], you can only display the value, not edit it. That's why I asked if you want to just display the value on the web server or also make changes through the web server.
Have you tested this recently? I was able to change the value successfully using the extended web server in the last few minutes. Of course, 'writable' must be checked.

Yes, I have tested it as well. I know the 'writable' checkbox must be set. You can set the checkbox, but changing the values via the web server doesn't actually work. Have you really tried changing them through the web server?
Oh, sorry, my mistake. Yes, [user_name]'s statement is correct.

I want users to be able to enter values from seconds to minutes, like 00:00 m. Is it possible to change the time unit from minutes to hours—such as 00:00 m to 00:00 h—directly through the browser? I will test it and report back.

analysis.insight_summary: Participants discussed how to create and visualize asynchronous pulse generators in the [product_name] Web Editor. Key usability findings include the limitations in time formatting and challenges with editing versus just displaying values through the interface. There was initial confusion about what the web server allows, but user feedback clarified recent improvements and ongoing issues, such as not being able to freely switch between minute and hour display units directly in the browser.
analysis.user_expectations: The user hopes to display and modify pulse durations using mm:ss or hh:mm formats in the web interface and wants the flexibility to switch between minute and hour units through the browser.
